item.title: $4 Million Settlement in Suit Against Officer Who Took Nude Images From Women’s Phones
item.description: Julian Alcala, who was a police officer in Eastern Missouri, had illegally obtained the private images during traffic stops, the authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner
item.media:description: Julian Alcala had been employed by the police department in Florissant, Mo., for 11 months, during which time he illegally obtained nude images from women during traffic stops, officials said.

item.title: Officer Charged With Violating Privacy for Recording Colleagues’ Racism
item.description: The charges stem from recordings that Daniel Flores made over the course of 2024, when he was working in a Los Angeles police unit that recruited new officers.
item.dc:creator: Jill Cowan and Shawn Hubler
item.category: Wiretapping and Other Eavesdropping Devices and Methods
item.media:description: After The Los Angeles Times reported on the recordings last year, the Police Department opened an internal investigation, and the taped remarks were denounced across the board by city leaders.

item.title: George Santos Fined Over Bets on State of the Union on Kalshi Prediction Market

item.title: Trump Administration Plans to Upend Head Start by Deregulating It

item.title: John Ali, Nation of Islam Official Who Clashed With Malcolm X, Dies at 98
item.description: He was widely suspected of being an F.B.I. informant and of playing a role in the 1965 assassination of Malcolm, the charismatic Black activist.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:description: John Ali, back row center, the Nation of Islam’s de facto second-in-command, stands behind the group’s leader, Elijah Muhammad, and between Jabir Herbert Muhammad, left, Mr. Muhammad’s son, and James Shabazz during a news conference after the assassination of Malcolm X in February 1965.

item.title: Todd Blanche’s Loyalty to Trump Is Putting His Attorney General Confirmation at Risk
item.description: Todd Blanche’s approach has collided with the jury-of-two reality in the Senate that has, thus far, kept him from the prize he covets: the stability and status conferred by a Senate confirmation.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush
item.media:description: Todd Blanche, according to current and former officials, understands that coping with President Trump’s demands, rages and U-turns is the price to pay for rising in his orbit.
